title: The v6 UI in the product: Chat is Home, a Dashboard per project, five project tabs, a hidden Library, Google Sans Flex, and every browser check passing
request: The owner rejected v3 (cream and terracotta, the Claude app's own look) and three original v4 looks, then gave a dashboard screenshot as the style to follow, with a warmer background. After v5 (that style on every page) the owner asked: Home becomes each project's dashboard, Chat becomes Home, the Library is hidden by a comment, the owner's example pages (More tools, Workflow agents, Project overview, Experiment results) are used in that style, nothing is crowded, and no existing function is removed: everything must work with the frontend and backend. Then: use Google Sans for all text. Then: fix the browser checks that failed.
spec: Demo v6 (docs/ui-demos/v6) built into dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src: the menu is Home (the chat), Projects and Agent, with Project tools and Operations under More tools; a project's pages are five tabs (Dashboard, Workflow, Data, Models, Brief) with a page picker; a new Projects list and a per-project Dashboard read only what the server already returns; the Library pages stay but are left out of the menu and search; the look is a warm ground, white soft cards, pill tabs, green actions with dark text and framed tables; one open font for all text. Every browser check, product flow and frontend test passes.
plan: Iterate on standalone demos first (v4, v5, v6 in docs/ui-demos), so the owner approves a direction before product code changes.
List every product page and its functions, and map each to a place in v6 (the demo's 'Where everything went' page), so nothing is lost.
Change the look through the Data science mode's tokens and one appended layer in ds.css, not page by page.
Restructure navigation in core.js (NAV, PROJECT_GROUPS, projectBar) and add two read-only views.
Run the build, the unit tests, the product flows and the browser suite; compare the browser suite with a baseline copy of the code before the change to separate new failures from old ones.
Have the dclab-reviewer agent review the diff, fix its findings, then fix the failures that were already there.

decisions.decision: Restyle through tokens and one appended CSS layer instead of rewriting 22 views.
decisions.why: The views hold about 13,000 lines and every function; changing their markup risks breaking behaviour, while the existing classes (panel, stat, btn, pill, ptabs, table.data) take a new look safely.

decisions.decision: Group project pages into five tabs with a page picker, keeping each page's own section tabs.
decisions.why: The owner asked for an uncrowded page without removing functions; five tabs plus a picker hold all eleven project pages.

decisions.decision: Hide the Library by commenting its menu group and filtering it from search (HIDDEN_VIEWS), keeping its pages and routes.
decisions.why: The owner said 'comment and hide it'; links from other pages (the brief, the Evidence chips) still open it.

decisions.decision: Use Google Sans Flex, self-hosted, instead of Google Sans.
decisions.why: Google Sans is proprietary; Google Sans Flex is its open version under the SIL Open Font License, and the app's CSP allows fonts from its own folder only. The download was approved by the owner.

decisions.decision: Show The team again on Home and keep the project switcher on Home.
decisions.why: The 2026-11-04 rule hid them in Data science while Developer kept them; Developer was removed, so hiding them removed the functions.

decisions.decision: Prove which browser failures were new by running the suite on a baseline worktree (HEAD plus the other session's uncommitted files, without this change).
decisions.why: The tree held another session's unfinished UI work; without a baseline, old failures would be blamed on this change or new ones hidden among them.

change: dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/core.js (chat icon; NAV: Home, Projects, Agent, More tools as Project tools and Operations, the Knowledge group commented out; HIDDEN_VIEWS kept out of search; PROJECT_GROUPS and projectBar painted from show(); recents open a project's dashboard; setNavCount finds counts anywhere in the sidebar); views/projects.html and views/dashboard.html (new, read GET /api/workspace and the open project); shell.html (#pbar); build.py (the two views); ds.css (v6 tokens, the v6 layer, Google Sans Flex for all text but code, the switcher and The team on Home, a slim header with an open chat); styles.css and fonts/ (Google Sans Flex with its licence); views/home.html (the team button waits for the agent; the activity log reads the project's transitions instead of a /steps call that always answered 422); scripts/browser_e2e.py (new views, v6 checks, task-plan setup, Dashboard follows the switcher, the dashboard in the unreadable check); tests/test_web_client.py; docs/ui-demos v2 to v6 with a README.

findings.defect: Delete confirm buttons became white text on light grey.
findings.scenario: Workflow, Delete, the modal's 'Delete the project' button (and Delete the session on the Agent page) in the light theme.
findings.cause: The new rule for plain buttons (.btn:not(.primary):not(.ghost)) outweighed .btn.danger.solid, and a later line forced white text.
findings.fix: The plain-button rule leaves .danger and .proof alone; the white-text line was removed.
findings.test: Checked in the running app; the browser suite's pages check covers the pages without errors.

findings.defect: The Dashboard said the final test was read once after it was reopened.
findings.scenario: A final stage rerun with a written reason makes holdout_uses 2; the card said 'Read once'.
findings.cause: Any non-zero count was drawn as once.
findings.fix: Sealed, Read once, or Read N times with a warning pill.
findings.test: Read in the code; the dashboard shows the count the project records.

findings.defect: The switch browser check read a sidebar project label that no longer exists.
findings.scenario: make browser-test on a workspace with a project.
findings.cause: The new menu has no project group.
findings.fix: The check reads the Dashboard's title after switching.
findings.test: switch passes in the full browser run.

findings.defect: A waiting question on Projects did not open its own chat.
findings.scenario: An open draft with an unanswered question, clicked on Projects.
findings.cause: The link went to #home without naming the draft.
findings.fix: It sets DC.state.resumeDraft before opening Home.
findings.test: Code path shared with the sidebar's recents.

findings.defect: Live job counts in the menu were lost.
findings.scenario: A running stage; Compute's count never appeared.
findings.cause: setNavCount looked only inside #nav and Compute moved to More tools without a count.
findings.fix: Counts on Compute and Agent; setNavCount searches the whole sidebar.

findings.defect: The new green text was below 4.5:1 on white.
findings.scenario: Links and ok text on cards.
findings.fix: #237A2D for text and ink (about 5.3:1); the bright green stays for button backgrounds with dark text.

findings.defect: The project switcher could not be reached on Home (decide, switch, memory, review failed).
findings.scenario: Open Home with a project; the green switcher is hidden, and hidden entirely while a chat is open.
findings.cause: Data science CSS hid Home's header actions, and the whole header with an open chat.
findings.fix: Home keeps only the switcher, centered; with a chat open the header shrinks to it.
findings.test: decide, switch, memory and review pass.

findings.defect: The team walk could not be used (team failed).
findings.scenario: Describe a problem on Home and start; The team never appears; once shown, Walk with the team is refused while the agent answers.
findings.cause: Two hiding rules (the 2026-11-04 rule and the open-chat rule), then a button enabled while the server refuses a walk with 409.
findings.fix: The team card shows above the chat; the button is disabled while the agent is answering.
findings.test: team passes: 5 questions, 1 confirmation, the build approved.

findings.defect: Home called GET /api/projects/{id}/steps with neither a stage nor a decision; the server answered 422 every time and the activity log never had the project's moves.
findings.scenario: Open Home after a project ran its stages; the console shows a 422.
findings.cause: The inspector added on 2026-11-15 (22ad1bf8) used /steps for the project's moves.
findings.fix: The log reads the project's transitions, which the project document already carries.
findings.test: decide passes with no console error.

findings.defect: The task-plan check expected 'preview is off' while execution was on.
findings.cause: Execution has been on by default since 426c76aa (2026-11-13); the check turned off only the preview.
findings.fix: The check turns both off for the read-only preview case.

findings.defect: test_web_client expected a list of browser checks without 'unreadable'.
findings.cause: d8814abb added the check without updating the test.
findings.fix: The name is in the expected set.

findings.defect: Models was 3 px wider than a 375 px phone, and project tabs scrolled out of sight.
findings.cause: Five project tabs in one row.
findings.fix: Below 560 px the tabs wrap and the picker takes the full width.

measurements.name: browser suite (make browser-test, installed Chrome)
measurements.result: Baseline before the change: 9 of 18 failing. After v6 and the review fixes: 9 failing, 7 the same as the baseline and the rest timing or the fixed overflow. After the Home fixes: 18 of 18 pass.
measurements.next: Run it again at the nightly gate.
limits: Playwright's own Chromium is not installed here; the suite ran with DCLAB_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome.
poll and the notebook's refusal failed once each, depending on the order of earlier checks, and passed in the last full run.

measurements.name: product flows (make product-e2e)
measurements.result: upload, upload-team, no-data, synthetic and log-file pass, before and after the Home fixes.
limits: No model: the flows run with DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS=1.

outcome: The product shows v6: Chat is Home, Projects and a Dashboard per project, five project tabs with a page picker, More tools with Project tools and Operations, the Library hidden but kept, Google Sans Flex for all text but code. Every browser check, product flow and frontend test passes.
lessons: A hiding rule written for one of two looks becomes a removed feature when the other look is deleted: when a mode goes, review what the remaining mode hid.
When a tree holds someone else's unfinished work, run the suite on a baseline worktree before blaming or excusing a failure.
A check that passes alone and fails in the full run depends on what earlier checks left behind; log failed requests (response status >= 400) to find the one request.
Count a reviewer's findings as part of the package: two of six were visible only with a destructive modal or a reopened holdout.
risks: The Library pages are reachable only from links inside other pages until the owner shows them again.
The team card above an open chat takes vertical room on small screens.
This commit also carries another session's uncommitted Home and Data science work, which this package tested but did not write.
